analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses why Hepatitis B virus (HBV) e antigen (HBeAg) induces macrophage activation and immune tolerance, a process linked to viral immune escape, while the spatial 3D genomic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying macrophage dysfunction remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study integrated RNA-sequencing, high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C), and chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing (ChIP-seq) to analyze control and HBeAg-stimulated macrophages, with key findings cross-validated using human HBV-infected datasets.
analysis.methods: RNA-sequencing, Hi-C, and ChIP-sequencing were used to map the topological and transcriptional regulatory landscape in macrophages exposed to HBeAg, including analyses of chromatin compartment switching, enhancer accumulation, topologically associating domain (TAD) restructuring, and epigenetic reprogramming.
analysis.main_results: HBeAg robustly activated pro-inflammatory transcriptional programs, particularly the TNF signaling pathway, accompanied by global 3D chromatin reorganization, including inactive-to-active compartment switching, de novo H3K27ac enhancer accumulation, TAD merging, and targeted intrachromosomal loop disruption affecting genes such as MET, FHOD3, FLNB, SESN2, KBTBD11, and BLVRB.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that HBeAg orchestrates a coordinated hierarchical restructuring of the 3D genome and targeted epigenetic reprogramming to induce macrophage dysfunction, identifying structural variants and core spatial-target genes (e.g., MET, FLNB, BLVRB) as novel mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the identified epigenetic and structural mechanisms or the implicated genes may offer therapeutic strategies for HBV-related liver diseases by modulating macrophage dysfunction and immune tolerance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro macrophage models and cross-validation with human HBV-infected datasets, leaving uncertainty about the direct applicability of these mechanisms in vivo and the clinical relevance of the identified targets.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Hepatitis B virus e antigen (HBeAg) drives macrophage activation and immune tolerance, a process implicated in viral immune escape, by mapping the 3D genomic and epigenetic changes in macrophages. Using RNA-sequencing, Hi-C, and ChIP-sequencing, the authors demonstrate that HBeAg induces global chromatin reorganization, including compartment switching, enhancer accumulation, and topologically associating domain restructuring, alongside targeted epigenetic reprogramming. These changes activate pro-inflammatory pathways such as TNF signaling while upregulating genes like MET and FLNB and downregulating genes like BLVRB. The study proposes that this coordinated 3D genome restructuring and epigenetic reprogramming underlies macrophage dysfunction, offering potential therapeutic targets for HBV-related liver diseases. However, the findings are derived from in vitro models and require validation in vivo to confirm their clinical relevance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解释了为什么乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) e 抗原 (HBeAg) 会诱导巨噬细胞激活和免疫耐受,这一过程与病毒免疫逃逸有关,而巨噬细胞功能障碍背后的空间 3D 基因组和表观遗传机制仍知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究整合了 RNA 测序、高通量染色体构象捕获 (Hi-C) 和染色质免疫沉淀测序 (ChIP-seq) 来分析对照和 HBeAg 刺激的巨噬细胞,并使用人类 HBV 感染数据集对关键发现进行了交叉验证。
elements_zh.methods: RNA 测序、Hi-C 和 ChIP 测序用于绘制暴露于 HBeAg 的巨噬细胞的拓扑和转录调控图谱,包括染色质区室转换、增强子积累、拓扑关联域 (TAD) 重组和表观遗传重编程的分析。
elements_zh.main_results: HBeAg 强烈激活促炎转录程序,特别是 TNF 信号通路,伴随着全局 3D 染色质重组,包括非活性到活性区室转换、从头 H3K27ac 增强子积累、TAD 合并以及影响 MET、FHOD3、FLNB、SESN2、KBBTD11 和 BLVRB 等基因的靶向染色体内环破坏。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HBeAg 协调协调 3D 基因组的层次结构重组和有针对性的表观遗传重编程,以诱导巨噬细胞功能障碍,识别结构变异和核心空间目标基因(例如 MET、FLNB、BLVRB)作为新的机制见解和潜在的治疗靶点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对已确定的表观遗传和结构机制或相关基因可能通过调节巨噬细胞功能障碍和免疫耐受为 HBV 相关肝病提供治疗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外巨噬细胞模型以及与人类 HBV 感染数据集的交叉验证,这使得这些机制在体内的直接适用性以及已确定目标的临床相关性存在不确定性。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)e抗原(HBeAg)在诱导巨噬细胞激活和随后的免疫耐受中发挥着关键作用,从而促进病毒免疫逃逸。然而,驱动这种巨噬细胞功能障碍的潜在空间 3D 基因组和表观遗传机制仍然很大程度上未知。方法 为了绘制拓扑和转录调控图谱,我们集成了 RNA 测序 (RNA-seq)、高通量染色体构象捕获 (Hi-C) 和染色质免疫沉淀测序 (ChIP-seq),以全面分析对照和 HBeAg 刺激的巨噬细胞。使用人类 HBV 感染数据集对主要发现进行了交叉验证。结果 HBeAg 强烈激活促炎转录程序,突出以 TNF 信号通路为中心节点。Hi-C 分析揭示了伴随这种表型转变的深刻的全局 3D 染色质重组。具体来说,非活性到活性(B 到 A)区室的转换,加上 H3K27ac 增强子的从头积累,直接驱动了 MET 和 FHOD3 等功能基因的上调。此外,拓扑关联域(TAD)重组,特别是 TAD 合并,暴露了新的调控元件来上调 FLNB 和 SESN2。相反,特定染色体内环的破坏导致 KBTBD11 和 BLVRB 等基因的定向下调。从机制上讲,靶向表观遗传重编程驱动了这种 3D 结构重新布线:AP-1/STAT 基序的 H3K27ac 增强子沉积富集,CTCF 与 FOX 家族因子协调改变结构边界,HLTF 介导靶向 H3K27me3 相关基因沉默。结论 HBeAg 协调 3D 基因组的高度协调的层次结构重组和有针对性的表观遗传重编程以诱导巨噬细胞功能障碍。已确定的结构变异和核心空间靶基因(如 MET、FLNB 和 BLVRB)提供了新的机制见解,并代表了 HBV 相关肝病的潜在治疗靶点。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解释了为什么乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) e 抗原 (HBeAg) 会诱导巨噬细胞激活和免疫耐受,这一过程与病毒免疫逃逸有关,而巨噬细胞功能障碍背后的空间 3D 基因组和表观遗传机制仍知之甚少。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究整合了 RNA 测序、高通量染色体构象捕获 (Hi-C) 和染色质免疫沉淀测序 (ChIP-seq) 来分析对照和 HBeAg 刺激的巨噬细胞,并使用人类 HBV 感染数据集对关键发现进行了交叉验证。
analysis_zh.methods: RNA 测序、Hi-C 和 ChIP 测序用于绘制暴露于 HBeAg 的巨噬细胞的拓扑和转录调控图谱,包括染色质区室转换、增强子积累、拓扑关联域 (TAD) 重组和表观遗传重编程的分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: HBeAg 强烈激活促炎转录程序,特别是 TNF 信号通路,伴随着全局 3D 染色质重组,包括非活性到活性区室转换、从头 H3K27ac 增强子积累、TAD 合并以及影响 MET、FHOD3、FLNB、SESN2、KBBTD11 和 BLVRB 等基因的靶向染色体内环破坏。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HBeAg 协调协调 3D 基因组的层次结构重组和有针对性的表观遗传重编程,以诱导巨噬细胞功能障碍,识别结构变异和核心空间目标基因(例如 MET、FLNB、BLVRB)作为新的机制见解和潜在的治疗靶点。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对已确定的表观遗传和结构机制或相关基因可能通过调节巨噬细胞功能障碍和免疫耐受为 HBV 相关肝病提供治疗策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外巨噬细胞模型以及与人类 HBV 感染数据集的交叉验证,这使得这些机制在体内的直接适用性以及已确定目标的临床相关性存在不确定性。

news.content: Search HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER MOBILE Global EditionASIA 中文双语Français HOME CHINA WORLD BUSINESS CULTURE TRAVEL VIDEO SPORTS OPINION REGIONAL NEWSPAPER China Daily PDF China Daily E-paper MOBILE China News Society Innovation HK/Macao Cross-Strait Cover Story Photo Environment Health Military Video Home / China / Society Home China Society Health campaign spotlights hepatitis B prevention across all ages chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-07-19 18:38 Share Share - WeChat CLOSE Runners are seen during a health campaign to control and eliminate hepatitis B in Beijing on Saturday. [Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn] With four years remaining until the 2030 target for eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat domestically, public health officials and clinicians gathered in Beijing to assess progress and map out next steps in hepatitis B control. Hepatitis B remains a major public health challenge in China. An estimated 75 million people aged 1 to 69 are living with chronic HBV infection, accounting for roughly one-third of global cases. A significant proportion of those infected are unaware of their status. The virus is highly contagious, and chronic infection can progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Since the introduction of universal free infant vaccination in 2005, coverage rates have climbed to 99.6% for the three-dose series and 95.6% for the timely birth dose—well above the global average of 85%. As a result, the prevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen among children under five has dropped to 0.30%, down from much higher levels in the 1990s. Among the broader population aged 1 to 69, the prevalence now stands at 5.86%. These achievements do not mark the finish line. In September 2025, the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and eight other government departments jointly issued an action plan for As part of the 2025–2030 action plan for addressing the disease, efforts to maintain high childhood vaccination rates while expanding adult immunization coverage are in full swing. Yao Fengli, deputy chief pediatrician at the Fifth Medical Center of the People's Liberation Army General Hospital, said that infants infected with HBV face a 90% risk of developing chronic infection, with long-term risks of cirrhosis and liver cancer. She urged that newborns should receive their first vaccine dose promptly after birth, followed by doses at one month and six months of age. As children enter preschool and school settings, group activities and close contact increase the risk of horizontal transmission. Parents should monitor their children's antibody levels and consult healthcare providers about screening and booster doses when necessary. Lyv Sa, senior physician at the Fifth Medical Center of the People's Liberation Army General Hospital’s liver disease department, said that HBV is not transmitted through everyday contact such as handshakes, hugging, shared meals, or attending classes together. She called for reducing stigma and encouraging family members of those infected to know their immune status and take appropriate preventive measures. Zhang Ying, chief physician at the Tianjin CDC, said that grassroots health centers play a critical role in delivering health education, on-site screening, vaccination reminders, and standardized follow-up care. analysis.brief_en: China marked progress toward its 2030 goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat with a national campaign spotlighting hepatitis B prevention across all ages. Held in Beijing on July 18, 2026, the event brought together public health officials and clinicians to review advances since universal infant vaccination began in 2005. Coverage for the three-dose series now reaches 99.6%, and the timely birth dose is administered to 95.6% of newborns, contributing to a sharp decline in chronic infection among children under five to 0.30%. Despite these gains, an estimated 75 million people aged 1 to 69 live with chronic hepatitis B in China, and about 5.86% of this age group remains affected. Experts emphasized maintaining high childhood vaccination rates while expanding adult immunization and called for reducing stigma and increasing screening to reach the undiagnosed.

Newswise — Each year, millions of people live with chronic hepatitis B that slowly develops into cirrhosis. Once cirrhosis patients suffer decompensation issues including fluid buildup in the belly and dangerous esophageal bleeding, their risks of repeated hospital stays and early death rise sharply.Clinicians mostly judge liver risk through one-time liver blood tests, which miss gradual whole-body tissue changes that drive disease deterioration. In a study published in Hepatobiliary Communications, researchers from The First Hospital of Lanzhou University uncovered clear, stage-specific tissue patterns from standard CT scans to predict upcoming severe liver complications.“We found that visceral fat and muscle shifts carry totally different warning meaning based on how advanced a patient’s cirrhosis is,” shares co-lead author Xiaoyue Zhang. “For patients with compensated early-stage cirrhosis, gradual degeneration of visceral fat signals a significantly higher risk of complications, and for those who have already experienced severe hepatic decompensation events, persistent muscle wasting serves as the primary warning marker.”The researchers confirmed tracking long-term tissue shifts delivers much more accurate risk alerts than isolated examinations. “Above all, these fat and muscle changes can be spotted on routine abdominal CT scans that every cirrhosis patient already undergoes, with no extra expensive or invasive testing needed,” adds Zhang.According to senior and corresponding author Junfeng Li, the team’s findings addressed an unmet clinical demand in daily liver disease management. “Past research rarely split cirrhosis patients by disease stage to sort out these tissue warning signals,” explains Li. “This easy CT monitoring method allows clinicians to launch personalized nutritional and metabolic support early, effectively slowing liver damage and lifting long-term survival chances for hepatitis B cirrhosis patients.”###ReferencesDOI10.1016/j.hbc.2026.100003Original Source URLhttps://doi.org/10.1016/j.hbc.2026.100003Funding InformationThis work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant no. 82360132]; news.title_zh: CT 测量的脂肪和肌肉变化可预测慢性乙型肝炎相关肝硬化的严重肝脏并发症新闻明智 - 新闻明智
news.source_body_en: A study published in Hepatobiliary Communications by researchers from The First Hospital of Lanzhou University has revealed that changes in visceral fat and muscle, as measured by standard CT scans, can predict severe liver complications in patients with chronic hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. The research indicates that for patients in the early stages of cirrhosis, the gradual degeneration of visceral fat signals a higher risk of complications. In contrast, persistent muscle wasting serves as a primary warning marker for those who have already experienced severe hepatic decompensation events. These findings address a significant clinical need by utilizing routine abdominal CT scans, which are already part of standard care for cirrhosis patients, to monitor tissue changes without the need for additional expensive or invasive tests. The study suggests that early detection of these tissue changes can allow clinicians to provide personalized nutritional and metabolic support, thereby slowing liver damage and improving long-term survival chances for patients.
news.content_zh: 兰州大学第一医院研究人员在《肝胆通讯》上发表的一项研究表明,通过标准 CT 扫描测量的内脏脂肪和肌肉的变化可以预测慢性乙型肝炎相关肝硬化患者的严重肝脏并发症。研究表明,对于肝硬化早期患者来说,内脏脂肪的逐渐退化意味着出现并发症的风险更高。相比之下,持续性肌肉萎缩是那些已经经历过严重肝功能失代偿事件的人的主要警告标志。这些发现通过利用常规腹部 CT 扫描(已经成为肝硬化患者标准护理的一部分)来监测组织变化而无需额外的昂贵或侵入性测试,满足了重要的临床需求。该研究表明,早期检测这些组织变化可以让临床医生提供个性化的营养和代谢支持,从而减缓肝损伤并提高患者的长期生存机会。

news.content_title: WHO, UNICEF question India's newborn hepatitis B vaccine data despite strong overall coverage
news.content: WHO, UNICEF question India's newborn hepatitis B vaccine data despite strong overall coverage WHO and UNICEF have challenged India's official estimate for the hepatitis B birth dose given to newborns within 24 hours. The gap has raised concerns over coverage denominators even as India's routine childhood immunisation remains high. The World Health Organisation (WHO) and UNICEF have questioned India’s official estimates on newborn hepatitis B vaccination coverage, saying the country’s reported figures overstate the proportion of babies receiving the critical birth dose within 24 hours of delivery even as India continues to post high coverage for most routine childhood immunisations. The assessment is part of the latest WHO-UNICEF Estimates of National Immunisation Coverage (WUENIC), released on July 15, which said that while global immunisation services have continued to recover, millions of children still miss life-saving vaccines, particularly those given at birth or requiring completion of multi-dose schedules. For India, the sharpest divergence between official administrative data and the WHO-UNICEF estimate relates to the hepatitis B birth dose (HEPBB), which is recommended within the first 24 hours of birth. The vaccine is critical because hepatitis B virus can be transmitted from an infected mother to her baby during childbirth, leading to chronic infection in up to 90 percent of infected infants. Chronic hepatitis B substantially raises the risk of liver cirrhosis and liver cancer later in life, making timely birth-dose vaccination one of the most effective preventive interventions. The Indian government reported 92 percent coverage for the hepatitis B birth dose in 2025, which, like several other vaccines, is offered free of cost to infants under the Centre's Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP). The WHO and UNICEF estimated actual national coverage at only 70 percent, indicating that nearly three in every 10 newborns missed the vaccine within the recommended time window. The agencies noted that the reported 92 percent coverage reflected vaccinations achieved in only 76 percent of the intended target population after annualising coverage across the national birth cohort. The estimate has been marked as “Estimate challenged by: R-”, indicating that WHO and UNICEF consider the nationally reported administrative data inconsistent with their final estimate because of concerns over the reported coverage denominator and target population. The agencies also reported they are aware that India is conducting a new National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6 came out last month but was likely not factored in for the immunisation report card) and they will review its findings once the final results become available. India Today has reached out to the Union health ministry for its comments. This copy will be updated if and when a reply is received. STRONG COVERAGE REPORT Despite the disagreement over the hepatitis B birth dose, India’s routine immunisation programme continued to register high estimated coverage across most childhood vaccines in 2025. The first dose of the diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis (DTP1) vaccine reached an estimated 97 percent of surviving infants, suggesting that only about 3% of children remained “zero-dose” for routine immunisation. Coverage for the first dose of the measles-containing vaccine and the first dose of the rubella-containing vaccine stood at 98 percent each. Coverage was estimated at 97% for the third dose of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, while both the third dose of the DTP vaccine and the third dose of the hepatitis B vaccine reached 95 percent. The first dose of inactivated polio vaccine also achieved 95% coverage. Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and the final dose of rotavirus vaccine were each estimated at 91 percent. Among all vaccines, however, the hepatitis B birth dose recorded the largest proportion of missed children, with 30 percent of newborns not receiving the vaccine within 24 hours of birth. Globally, WHO and UNICEF estimated that 13.5 million children remained “zero-dose” in 2025, meaning they did not receive a single vaccine during their first year of life. While that represented nearly 750,000 fewer children than in 2024, the agencies cautioned that increasing numbers of children begin vaccinations but fail to complete the recommended schedule. The report also highlighted encouraging regional trends. Compared with pre-pandemic levels in 2019, the WHO South-East Asia Region, which includes India, has not only recovered but now records the highest immunisation performance among WHO regions. Africa, the Eastern Mediterranean and Europe have improved but remain below their pre-pandemic coverage levels, while the Western Pacific has experienced further declines and is now the furthest below its 2019 baseline

news.content_zh: 2026 年 7 月 15 日,世界卫生组织和联合国儿童基金会质疑印度对新生儿乙型肝炎疫苗接种覆盖率的官方估计,认为报告的 92% 覆盖率夸大了婴儿在分娩 24 小时内接受关键出生剂量的实际比例。这些机构估计全国实际覆盖率仅为70%,这表明近30%的新生儿错过了建议时间窗口内的疫苗接种。这种差异引起了人们对覆盖率分母和目标人群的担忧,因为疫苗对于预防慢性乙型肝炎至关重要,慢性乙型肝炎会显着增加以后患肝硬化和肝癌的风险。世卫组织和儿童基金会指出,他们了解印度正在进行的全国家庭健康调查(NFHS-6),并将在调查结果公布后对其进行审查。印度政府的评论尚未发表,《今日印度》已联系联邦卫生部寻求回应。

Despite the clinical significance of this chronic inflammatory state, the precise molecular mechanisms that initiate and sustain HBV-induced hepatic damage remain poorly understood. Related StoriesBlood test may predict which colorectal cancer patients benefit from chemotherapyUltrasensitive biosensor detects early-stage liver fibrosis using small amount of bloodDual-compartment monitoring strategy improves evaluation of donor human liversIn a recent Genes & Diseases study, researchers from Chongqing Medical University investigated the mechanisms underlying HBV-induced liver inflammation and identified a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent signaling cascade that activates the Jak2/Stat3 pathway, thereby triggering hepatic inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic analyses of HBV transgenic mice and liver samples from patients with chronic HBV infection revealed that early hepatic inflammation is characterized by pronounced suppression of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), particularly genes associated with mitochondrial respiratory complexes I and III, leading to mitochondrial respiratory dysfunction. Functional studies using HBV-replicating hepatocyte cell lines demonstrated that persistent viral replication progressively impaired mitochondrial respiration, resulting in elevated intracellular ROS production. This metabolic disturbance drives excessive accumulation of ROS within the hepatocytes. Similar mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress were observed in HBV replication mouse models during the early stages of liver inflammation, indicating that mitochondrial dysfunction and the resulting ROS accumulation represent initiating events in HBV-associated inflammatory responses. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that ROS accumulation activated the antioxidant regulator Nrf2, which subsequently enhanced the production of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-8. These cytokines stimulated phosphorylation of Jak2 and Stat3 without altering total protein expression, leading to transcriptional activation of multiple inflammatory genes, including Saa1, S100a9, Icam1, and Socs3, involved in immune cell recruitment and hepatic inflammation. Pharmacological manipulation of ROS levels further confirmed this mechanism, as ROS scavenging with Mito-TEMPO or suppression of HBV replication reduced Nrf2 activation, cytokine production, Jak2/Stat3 signaling, and inflammatory gene expression, whereas ROS induction produced the opposite effects. This mechanism was further validated in vivo using a pAAV/HBV1.2 mouse model with persistent HBV replication, where increased oxidative stress coincided with elevated Nrf2 expression, enhanced IL-6 and IL-8 production, activation of Jak2/Stat3 signaling, and infiltration of inflammatory cells within the liver. Treatment with the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) markedly reduced hepatic ROS accumulation, suppressed activation of the Jak2/Stat3 pathway, decreased inflammatory cytokine expression, and alleviated liver inflammation, demonstrating that oxidative stress is a critical upstream regulator of HBV-induced inflammatory responses. Collectively, this study establishes mitochondrial dysfunction-induced ROS accumulation as a pivotal trigger of HBV-associated hepatic inflammation through activation of the Nrf2-IL-6/IL-8-Jak2/Stat3 signaling axis. By linking viral replication to oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling, this study provides mechanistic insights into the early pathogenesis of chronic hepatitis B and identifies ROS-dependent Jak2/Stat3 activation as a promising therapeutic target for preventing inflammation-driven liver disease progression. analysis.brief_en: Researchers at Chongqing Medical University have uncovered a molecular mechanism linking chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to liver inflammation. Their study, published in Genes & Diseases on 17 July 2026, shows that HBV replication disrupts mitochondrial respiration in hepatocytes, causing a buildup of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This oxidative stress activates the antioxidant regulator Nrf2, which then stimulates production of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-8. news.content_zh: 重庆医科大学的研究人员发现了慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染与肝脏炎症之间的分子机制。他们的研究于 2026 年 7 月 17 日发表在《基因与疾病》杂志上,表明 HBV 复制会扰乱肝细胞中的线粒体呼吸,导致活性氧 (ROS) 积聚。这种氧化应激会激活抗氧化调节剂 Nrf2,然后刺激促炎细胞因子 IL-6 和 IL-8 的产生。这些细胞因子磷酸化并激活 Jak2/Stat3 信号通路,驱动 Saa1、S100a9、Icam1 和 Socs3 等炎症基因的转录。在 HBV 复制细胞系和 pAAV/HBV1.2 小鼠模型中进行的实验证实,用 Mito-TEMPO 或抗氧化剂 N-乙酰半胱氨酸清除 ROS 可减少 Jak2/Stat3 激活、细胞因子水平和肝脏炎症。这些发现将 ROS 依赖性 Jak2/Stat3 信号传导定位为潜在的治疗靶点,以防止炎症驱动的慢性乙型肝炎进展为肝硬化和肝癌。

news.content: Coroner raises concerns over lack of national guidance on prescribing for hepatitis B reactivation A patient died from complications from reactivation of hepatitis B, after the supply of viral reactivation prophylaxis was inadvertently discontinued. Patient safety 16 July 2026 By Sophie Willis Advertisement Copy link to page Download PDF The coroner wrote that although a “large population” of patients have been diagnosed with hepatitis B through opt-out screening in emergency departments, specialised commissioning is lacking to ensure engagement with services Olga Yastremska / Alamy Stock Photo A coroner has raised concerns over a lack of national guidance on prescribing and monitoring for hepatitis B reactivation, following the death of a patient. In a ‘ Prevention of future deaths’ report ‘, published online on 10 July 2026, Richard Brittain, assistant coroner for Inner London North, stated that patient Tung Tran, aged 41 years, died from complications from reactivation of hepatitis B, “which arose from inadvertent discontinuation of necessary medical treatment”. Tran had a renal transplant in 2013 and was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B during the process, the coroner wrote. The patient was later discharged from hepatology and continued to receive viral reactivation prophylaxis entecavir from renal transplant services. “Supply of medication changed to home delivery in early 2025 but the entecavir was inadvertently discontinued, as there was a presumption that hepatology would continue to prescribe this. Mr Tran appears to have understood this to have been an intentional change of his medication,” the coroner said. “He attended his local hospital in August 2025 with signs of acute liver disease from reactivation of hepatitis B and was transferred to the Royal Free Hospital. He was too unwell to be considered for liver transplant and sadly died on 12 September 2025.” Directing a concern over the risk of future deaths to the British Viral Hepatitis Group at the British Association for the Study of the Liver (BASL), the coroner noted: “There is a lack of national guidance regarding which services should be responsible for the monitoring and prescribing in relation to hepatitis B reactivation prevention.” He also directed a concern to the UK Health Security Agency that there is a “large population” of patients who have been found to have hepatitis B through opt-out screening in emergency departments, “but there is a lack of specialised commissioning to maintain subsequent engagement with services”. “I heard that this differs from the position with regards to hepatitis C and HIV services, even though these patient populations are smaller,” the coroner added. In its response to the report , sent on 6 July 2026, the BASL said: [The BASL] does not lead the development or publication of clinical guidelines.” Patients with chronic hepatitis B are “usually managed in specialist hepatology services and the responsibility of monitoring and prescribing lies with these services”, it added. The BASL continued that for patients at risk of reactivation of hepatitis B, guidance on antiviral therapy is provided by “the relevant specialist societies and also in local NHS trust guidance”. “There is variation between NHS trusts as to whether this monitoring and prescribing is delivered by the treating team or whether specialist hepatology services are involved,” it said. Read more: Hepatitis B — prevention, diagnosis and management Last updated 16 July 2026 14:33 Citation The Pharmaceutical Journal , PJ July 2026, Vol 320, No 8011;320(8011)::DOI:10.1211/PJ.2026.1.419732 Please leave a comment Cancel reply You must be logged in to post a comment. analysis.brief_en: A coroner in the UK has raised significant concerns over the lack of national guidance on prescribing and monitoring for hepatitis B reactivation, following the death of a 41-year-old patient, Tung Tran. Tran, who had a renal transplant in 2013 and was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B, died on 12 September 2025 from complications arising from the reactivation of hepatitis B due to the inadvertent discontinuation of necessary medical treatment. The coroner's report, published on 10 July 2026, highlighted that the supply of medication changed to home delivery in early 2025 but was discontinued under the presumption that hepatology services would continue prescribing. Tran was transferred to the Royal Free Hospital in August 2025 with signs of acute liver disease but was too unwell to be considered for a liver transplant. The coroner directed concerns to the British Viral Hepatitis Group at the British Association for the Study of the Liver (BASL) and the UK Health Security Agency, noting a lack of specialized commissioning to maintain engagement with services. BASL responded that they do not lead the development of clinical guidelines and that responsibilities vary between NHS trusts.

news.content_zh: 在 41 岁患者 Tung Tran 死亡后,英国验尸官对缺乏关于乙型肝炎重新激活的处方和监测的国家指导表示严重关切。Tran于2013年接受了肾移植,并被诊断出患有慢性乙型肝炎,由于无意中停止了必要的治疗,导致乙型肝炎重新激活而引起的并发症于2025年9月12日去世。验尸官于 2026 年 7 月 10 日发布的报告强调,药物供应在 2025 年初改为送货上门,但由于假设肝病服务将继续开处方而停止。2025 年 8 月,Tran 因出现急性肝病症状而被转移到皇家自由医院,但由于身体状况太差,无法考虑进行肝移植。验尸官向英国肝脏研究协会 (BASL) 的英国病毒性肝炎小组和英国健康安全局提出了担忧,指出缺乏专门的委托来维持与服务的接触。BASL 回应称,他们并不主导临床指南的制定,而且 NHS 信托机构之间的责任也有所不同。

news.content: Culture Economics Education In the world Sport Tourism Technologies Health Energy Society Transport WC-2026 Business Politics Culture Economics Education In the world Sport Tourism Technologies Health Energy Society Transport WC-2026 Business Politics Culture Economics Education In the world Sport Tourism Technologies Health All categories Main / News / Health 18.03.2025 13351 Share on social network WHO strengthens medical professionals’ capacity in Turkmenistan on viral hepatitis B The World Health Organization (WHO) Country Office in Turkmenistan held a training course on the "Diagnostics and treatment of viral hepatitis B according to WHO recommendations and national protocol" from March 12 to 13, 2025. The course led by WHO/Europe consultant, Professor Alexander Nersesov, aims to enhance the capacity of Turkmen medical professionals in their effort to combat viral hepatitis B. The skill-building session was conducted at the Infectious disease treatment-prevention center in videoconference mode. The participants of the event were doctors specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of viral hepatitis from the Infectious disease treatment-prevention center of the Directorate of Infectious Diseases Centers, primary health care providers, infectious diseases specialists from the institutions at the district level, and representatives from the department of infectious diseases at the State Medical University named after Myrat Karryev. The training covered essential information on hepatitis B, its diagnosis, classification, and treatment, with specific guidance for chronic cases, pregnancy, and special patient groups, as well as hepatitis D. This training is designed to equip medical professionals with the updated knowledge and best practices in viral hepatitis B diagnosis and treatment, aligning with both WHO guidelines and national protocols. By enhancing the skills of healthcare providers, this initiative will contribute to improved patient outcomes and strengthen Turkmenistan's efforts to control and manage viral hepatitis. news.title_zh: 世卫组织加强土库曼斯坦医疗专业人员应对乙型病毒性肝炎的能力 - Turkmenportal.com
news.source_body_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) Country Office in Turkmenistan held a training course on the "Diagnostics and treatment of viral hepatitis B according to WHO recommendations and national protocol" from March 12 to 13, 2025. Led by WHO/Europe consultant Professor Alexander Nersesov, the course aimed to enhance the capacity of Turkmen medical professionals in combating viral hepatitis B. The training, conducted at the Infectious disease treatment-prevention center in videoconference mode, covered essential information on hepatitis B, its diagnosis, classification, and treatment, including specific guidance for chronic cases, pregnancy, and special patient groups, as well as hepatitis D. Participants included doctors specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of viral hepatitis, primary health care providers, infectious diseases specialists, and representatives from the department of infectious diseases at the State Medical University named after Myrat Karryev. The initiative is expected to contribute to improved patient outcomes and strengthen Turkmenistan's efforts to control and manage viral hepatitis.
news.content_zh: 世界卫生组织驻土库曼斯坦国家办事处于2025年3月12日至13日举办了“根据世界卫生组织建议和国家方案诊断和治疗乙型病毒性肝炎”培训课程。该课程由世界卫生组织/欧洲顾问Alexander Nersesov教授主持,旨在提高土库曼斯坦医务人员抗击病毒性肝炎的能力。培训在传染病治疗和预防中心以视频会议方式进行,涵盖了基本知识有关乙型肝炎及其诊断、分类和治疗的信息,包括针对慢性病例、妊娠和特殊患者群体以及丁型肝炎的具体指导。参与者包括专门从事病毒性肝炎诊断和治疗的医生、初级卫生保健人员、传染病专家以及以 Myrat Karryev 命名的国立医科大学传染病系的代表。该倡议预计将有助于改善患者的治疗效果,并加强土库曼斯坦控制和管理病毒性肝炎的努力。
